contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside cub::BlockRadixSort, about 7 per 4-bit pass (ranking 2, BlockScan 2, exchange 2, between passes 1), 4 passes for bf16 and 8 for fp32, 26 BAR.SYNC in the latency kernel
contract.k_range: [1, N) at compile time, the sort is k independent
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT, IPT >= 1, N <= 32768, threads 128, 256 or 512 accepted, measured N 2048 at 256 threads in this card
contract.type_constraints: bf16 (32-bit word, twiddled key high, index low) and fp32 (64-bit word), int32 indices from the blocked position. Temp storage max(9216, (N + N/32) x word bytes): 9216 bf16 and 16896 fp32 at N 2048
contract.nan_behavior: twiddled bitwise, positive NaN above +inf, negative NaN below -inf, never in focus-set inputs. -0.0 folded onto +0.0 before twiddling
contract.tie_break_support: inherent through the stability of the LSD sort over the key bits with the input in index order, same binary for both requirements. The control B1_idx supports not_guaranteed only and was instantiated under not_guaranteed for the prefer_smaller_index cells (harness --control-req)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent at zero extra cost, slot r holds rank r

correctness.notes: Kill cell against the block incumbent B1_idx (index-only AIR radix select, not_guaranteed only): N 2048 k 1024, bf16 and fp32, both regimes, the prefer_smaller_index cells of the variant against B1_idx under not_guaranteed in the same lock section (label kill_b1, umbriel-b200-020, source commit 971a398f42). Full oracle battery passed in every cell for both requirements.

low_level: Same kernels as card B6_radix_b200_20261025_1 (bf16 56 registers, fp32 64, no spill, 26 BAR.SYNC, 1008 and 888 SASS instructions, shared memory 17472 and 25088 bytes with the harness's output buffers). B1_idx at the same cells: 2128 bytes of temp storage independent of N, 32 to 48 registers.
Throughput occupancy 4 blocks per SM for both B6 kernels at N 2048 (registers 62 to 64), canaries 32.00 cycles and 3776 us at both ends.
algorithmic: B6_radix against B1_idx at N 2048 k 1024: bf16 5550 against 2933 cycles (1.89x slower), fp32 13499 against 2869 (4.71x), throughput bf16 159 against 342 Gelem per s (0.47x), fp32 59 against 337 (0.18x). B1_idx is the weaker of the two controls at this cell (B3_tuned 2550 and 2509, its k-flat scan emission against B1's ticket epilogue), so the better control decides the kill: 2.18x and 5.37x against the 1.2x threshold.

Under prefer_smaller_index B6_radix gives the exact index-ordered set at the not_guaranteed price (5550.8 against 5550.8), where B1_idx has no deterministic path (B1_det costs plus 19 to 51 percent in wave 1). A sorted, deterministic output is the one thing the sort has over the incumbent, and at 1.9x the price it is the sorted-output row only.
negative: No cell of the kill batch is within the threshold against either control, the sort is not a selection primitive at k = N/2 (see card B6_radix_b200_20261025_1 for the N and k sweep against B3_tuned).
surprises: B1_idx's ticket epilogue at k 1024 costs it 15 percent against B3_tuned here (2933 against 2550) and still leaves it 1.9x ahead of the sort: the whole k dependence of the select is smaller than one radix sort pass.
open_questions: None specific to this pairing. The final evaluation pairs B3_tuned with B1_idx at these cells (N8 report section 4 did it at N 16384 and 32768), the sort does not enter that pairing.
